Case: Email or username field is autofocused when the identifier step loads
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. Browser supports autofocus.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC1
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Step 1 'Welcome back': one field 'Email or username', required, autofocus, autocomplete=email. (LG-01)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Observe the page once it finishes loading.
  3. Check which element has keyboard focus without clicking anything.
Expected:
• The page heading reads "Welcome back".
  • The "Email or username" field is focused immediately on page load — the cursor is active in the field without any user interaction.
  • The field has the autocomplete attribute set to email.
BDD: Given a signed-out user navigates to the login identifier page, When the page loads, Then the Email or username field is auto-focused

Case: Password step is displayed when a valid email address is submitted on the identifier step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. A valid, well-formed email address is available (account exists in SleekFlow).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC1, AC4
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Any well-formed email goes to the password step, whether or not an account exists (no enumeration). (LG-04)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Enter a valid, well-formed email address belonging to an existing account.
  3. Click Continue (or press Enter).
  4. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:
• The page transitions to Step 2 "Sign in to continue".
  • The password input field is visible.
  • The entered email address appears in a read-only identifier display.
  • No error message is shown.
BDD: Given a user enters a valid email for an existing account on the identifier step, When Continue is clicked, Then the password step is displayed

Case: Password step is displayed when a valid username is submitted on the identifier step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. A valid username (5–128 characters, allowed characters only) for an existing account is available.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC1, AC3
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Usernames: 5–128 characters; letters, digits and _ + - . ! # $ ^ ` ~ @ '. Checked server-side. (LG-03)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Enter a valid username (e.g., 8 alphanumeric characters) belonging to an existing account.
  3. Click Continue (or press Enter).
  4. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:
• The page transitions to the password step.
  • The username appears as the read-only identifier on the password step.
  • No validation error is shown.
BDD: Given a user enters a valid username on the identifier step, When Continue is clicked, Then the password step is displayed

Case: Required field error is shown when identifier step is submitted with an empty field
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. The email/username field is empty.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC2
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Empty submit shows 'Email address or username is required'. (LG-02)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Leave the Email or username field empty.
  3. Click Continue (or press Enter).
  4. Observe the error message.
Expected:
• The page does not advance to the password step.
  • The error message "Email address or username is required" appears below or near the field.
  • The field retains focus.
BDD: Given the email or username field is empty, When the user submits the identifier step, Then the error message 'Email address or username is required' is displayed

Case: Server-side error is shown when a username with disallowed characters or invalid length is submitted
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. Username to test: fewer than 5 characters, or containing a disallowed character (e.g., space, @@ double at, or bracket).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC3
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Usernames: 5–128 characters; letters, digits and _ + - . ! # $ ^ ` ~ @ '. Checked server-side. (LG-03)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Enter a username with fewer than 5 characters (e.g., "ab") and click Continue.
  3. Observe the error response.
  4. Return to the identifier step and enter a username with a disallowed character (e.g., "user name" with a space) and click Continue.
  5. Observe the error response.
Expected:
• Neither submission advances to the password step.
  • An error message is shown indicating the username is invalid or does not meet the character rules.
  • No account information is revealed in the error message.
BDD: Given a user enters a username that is too short or contains disallowed characters, When the form is submitted, Then a validation error is shown and the user stays on the identifier step

Case: Password step is displayed when a valid but non-existent email is submitted on the identifier step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. A well-formed email address that does NOT have a SleekFlow account is used.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC4
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Any well-formed email goes to the password step, whether or not an account exists (no enumeration). (LG-04)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Enter a valid, well-formed email address that does not belong to any existing SleekFlow account.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. Observe whether the user is advanced to the password step or shown an account-not-found error.
Expected:
• The page transitions to the password step — same as for an existing email.
  • No message such as "account not found" or "email not registered" is shown.
  • The response is indistinguishable from a valid existing account submission.
BDD: Given a user enters a well-formed email that has no SleekFlow account, When the identifier step is submitted, Then the password step is shown with no account enumeration error

Case: Sign-up link on the identifier step preserves the Auth0 session state and ui_locales parameters
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is not signed in. The login page was opened with valid state and ui_locales query parameters.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC5
  • Traceability / AC Source: "'Sign up' link keeps session state and ui_locales. (LG-05)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier ensuring the URL contains state and ui_locales parameters.
  2. Click the "Sign up" link on the page.
  3. Inspect the URL of the resulting sign-up page.
Expected:
• The sign-up page URL contains the same state parameter value as the original login URL.
  • The sign-up page URL contains the same ui_locales parameter value as the original login URL.
  • No Auth0 error is displayed on the sign-up page.
BDD: Given the login identifier page carries a valid state and ui_locales, When the Sign up link is clicked, Then the sign-up page URL preserves both parameters

Case: Product carousel is hidden or reflows below the form when viewport width is at or below 1000px
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the login identifier page on a browser that can be resized.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC6
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Left panel: 4-slide product carousel; moves below the form or hides at ≤ 1000 px. (LG-06)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier on a desktop browser.
  2. Confirm the 4-slide product carousel is visible in the left panel at viewport width > 1000px.
  3. Resize the browser window to exactly 1000px wide.
  4. Observe the carousel position and visibility.
  5. Resize further to 800px wide and observe again.
Expected:
• At viewport widths greater than 1000px, the 4-slide carousel is displayed in the left panel.
  • At viewport width ≤ 1000px, the carousel either disappears entirely or moves below the login form.
  • The login form remains fully usable at narrow widths.
BDD: Given a user views the login page on a narrow viewport, When the width is at or below 1000px, Then the product carousel moves below the form or hides

Case: Password step displays correct UI elements including read-only identifier, Edit link, show/hide toggle, Reset password link, and Keep me signed in checkbox
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has completed the identifier step with a valid email or username and is now on the password step.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC7
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Step 2 'Sign in to continue': identifier read-only with 'Edit'; password with show/hide; 'Reset password' link; 'Keep me signed in' ticked by default; no social buttons. (LG-07)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier and submit a valid identifier to reach the password step.
  2. Inspect the page heading.
  3. Confirm the identifier is shown as read-only text with an adjacent Edit link.
  4. Confirm the password field has a show/hide visibility toggle.
  5. Confirm a "Reset password" link is present.
  6. Confirm "Keep me signed in" checkbox is present and checked by default.
  7. Confirm no Google or Apple social login buttons are shown on this step.
Expected:
• Page heading reads "Sign in to continue".
  • The identifier (email or username) is displayed as read-only text.
  • An "Edit" link is visible next to the identifier.
  • The password field includes a show/hide eye-icon toggle.
  • A "Reset password" link is present on the page.
  • "Keep me signed in" checkbox is visible and checked by default.
  • No Google or Apple login buttons appear on the password step.
BDD: Given a user has submitted a valid identifier, When the password step loads, Then all required UI elements are present and correctly configured

Case: Identifier step is restored when the Edit link is clicked on the password step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has advanced to the password step after entering an identifier.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC7
  • Traceability / AC Source: "identifier read-only with 'Edit' (LG-07)"
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login identifier step and submit a valid identifier to reach the password step.
  2. Click the "Edit" link next to the read-only identifier.
  3. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:
• The user is taken back to the identifier step (Step 1).
  • The previously entered identifier is pre-populated in the email/username field.
  • The Auth0 session state is maintained (no invalid_request error).
BDD: Given a user is on the password step, When the Edit link is clicked, Then the identifier step is displayed with the previous identifier pre-filled

Case: Password text is revealed and masked when the show/hide toggle is clicked on the password step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password step and has typed a password.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC7
  • Traceability / AC Source: "password with show/hide (LG-07)"
Test Steps:
1. Advance to the password step by submitting a valid identifier.
  2. Type any password into the password field.
  3. Click the show/hide toggle icon.
  4. Observe whether the password text is now visible.
  5. Click the toggle again.
  6. Observe whether the password is masked again.
Expected:
• After clicking the toggle once, the password characters are displayed as plain text.
  • After clicking the toggle again, the password characters are masked (shown as dots or asterisks).
BDD: Given a user has typed a password on the password step, When the show/hide toggle is clicked, Then the password is revealed as plain text, and clicking again masks it

Case: Required field error is shown when the password step is submitted with an empty password
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the password step. The password field is empty.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC8
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Empty password submit shows 'Password is required'. (LG-08)"
Test Steps:
1. Advance to the password step by submitting a valid identifier.
  2. Leave the password field empty.
  3. Click the "Sign in" button.
  4. Observe the error message.
Expected:
• The page does not advance beyond the password step.
  • The error message "Password is required" appears below or near the password field.
BDD: Given the password field is empty on the password step, When Sign in is clicked, Then the error message 'Password is required' is displayed

Case: Generic error message is shown when an incorrect password is entered on the password step
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has a valid SleekFlow account. User is on the password step for that account.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC9
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Wrong password shows a generic error; repeated failures are throttled. (LG-09) [TBD: exact error message text — LG-09 is assumed]"
Test Steps:
1. Advance to the password step by submitting a valid registered email.
  2. Enter an incorrect password.
  3. Click "Sign in".
  4. Observe the error message displayed.
  5. Confirm the error message does not reveal whether the account exists or the reason for failure beyond "wrong credentials".
Expected:
• Login fails and the user remains on the password step.
  • A generic error message is displayed (exact text TBD per open item LG-09).
  • The error message does not reveal account existence or specific failure reason beyond invalid credentials.
BDD: Given a user enters an incorrect password for a valid account, When Sign in is clicked, Then a generic error message is shown without disclosing account details

Case: Login is throttled after repeated incorrect password attempts
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has a valid SleekFlow account. Lockout threshold is unknown (TBD per open item). NOTE: Exact threshold and throttled-state UI not yet specified.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC9
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Wrong password shows a generic error; repeated failures are throttled. (LG-09) [TBD: Lockout threshold — how many failed attempts before throttling? What does throttled state look like?]"
Test Steps:
1. Advance to the password step for a valid registered account.
  2. Enter an incorrect password and click Sign in — repeat this action multiple times in succession (e.g., 5–10 times).
  3. Observe whether the login form becomes temporarily unavailable or rate-limited.
  4. Observe any message or UI change indicating throttling.
Expected:
• After a number of consecutive failed password attempts, the login form is throttled (rate-limited).
  • A message or UI indicator informs the user that too many attempts have been made.
  • Further immediate login attempts are blocked or delayed.
BDD: Given a user makes repeated incorrect password submissions, When the threshold is exceeded, Then the login flow is throttled and further attempts are blocked or rate-limited

Case: Two-factor authentication code step is presented after correct password when 2FA is enforced for the user role
Description:
• Pre-condition: A SleekFlow company account has 2FA enforcement enabled for the test user's role. The user has a valid authenticator app set up.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC10
  • Traceability / AC Source: "If the company enforces 2FA for the user's role: 6-digit authenticator code after the password. (LG-10)"
Test Steps:
1. Advance to the password step using credentials for a user whose company enforces 2FA for their role.
  2. Enter the correct password and click Sign in.
  3. Observe whether a 2FA step appears.
  4. Enter the current 6-digit code from the authenticator app.
  5. Observe the resulting page.
Expected:
• After correct password entry, the page advances to a 2FA screen (not directly to the dashboard).
  • The 2FA screen requests a 6-digit authenticator code.
  • Entering the correct 6-digit code results in successful login and dashboard access.
BDD: Given a user's company enforces 2FA for their role and the correct password is entered, When Sign in is clicked, Then the 6-digit authenticator code step is presented

Case: Dashboard is displayed after successful login with valid credentials and 2FA code
Description:
• Pre-condition: User has a valid SleekFlow account with 2FA enabled. Authenticator app is available. Browser session has no active login.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-001 · AC1, AC7, AC10
  • Traceability / AC Source: Full login flow: identifier → password → 2FA → dashboard. Context: "Login is a multi-step flow: identifier → password → optional 2FA → dashboard."
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier.
  2. Enter a valid email and click Continue.
  3. Enter the correct password and click Sign in.
  4. When the 2FA screen appears, enter the current 6-digit code from the authenticator app.
  5. Observe the page after submitting the code.
Expected:
• The user is successfully redirected to the SleekFlow dashboard (app home page).
  • No error messages are shown at any step.
  • The user's workspace is accessible.
BDD: Given a user with valid credentials and 2FA completes all login steps correctly, When the final step is submitted, Then the user arrives at the SleekFlow dashboard
